title: AI agent maps proton-gated water loss in perrhenate-catalysed deoxydehydration
summary: The paper reports a computational mechanism for perrhenate-catalysed deoxydehydration: proton-assisted water loss enables ring closure and alcohol reduction. Under human-defined hypotheses, a Claude Code agent located transition states, which the authors validated. Coupled-cluster-anchored microkinetic modeling predicted a rate increase of about eight orders of magnitude over the best proton-free pathway. At matched conversion conditions, modeled barriers were consistent with the 31.5–34.0 kcal/mol window inferred from previously reported experimental turnover; this was not a new wet-lab demonstration.
ai_technology: Claude Code LLM agent for human-directed reaction-network and transition-state search, combined with electronic-structure calculations and microkinetic modeling

evidence.tested: Agent-located transition states verified by the authors; computed energetics, reaction-network and microkinetic consistency checks; comparisons to existing turnover-derived barrier estimates.
evidence.unknown: Main paper reviewed; supplementary files were not read. The mechanism and rate changes are predictions compared with prior experimental kinetics, not a new experimental confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Code carried out calculation/search/triage workflows for author-specified mechanistic hypotheses; authors validated the located stationary points.
